candidateIdentity: sourceHash identifies the measured production file; committed evidence cannot contain its own commit hash
method: Five serial baseline/candidate pairs; fixture v1; 64 warmup, 4096 measured appends per history; CPU timing separate from HeapProfiler sampling at 1024 bytes with collected objects included. Deterministic/WeakRef checks are separate from profiling. Existing histories are loaded before timing; history=0 is an already-flushed header, not initial installation.
limits: Native appendFileSync opens/closes are internal to Node; baseline explicitOpens=0 is not a syscall count.
Windows process CPU accounting is coarse; wall p95 includes filesystem/OS latency. The 1000-history wall p95 rose 5.59% (6.1 microseconds). No claim of stable timing improvement.
Allocation samples include Node and inspector overhead; they are estimates, not exact object counts.
Lifecycle observes the entry and its 1 MiB logical message payload through WeakRef; it does not equate string length with physical heap bytes.

Initial atomic install helper remains unchanged; fd ownership counters apply to steady append. Exception handling, first flush and explicit reload are verified by fault tests, not regular-frame allocation budgets.
